79624.body:
----------
_**Your Weekly Deep Dive into The World of Crypto**_

**September 23, 2026 · ****5 Min Read**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b41cd04a-38ae-4dd8-ad93-eabf03bc2f58/image.png?t=1790142576)
Caption: _As of September 23, 2026, Morning ET  |  Sources: CoinGecko, Alternative.me, SoSoValue_

## 📡** THIS WEEK IN CRYPTO**

**GM, Readers!**

The twin catalysts landed. Bitcoin shrugged. The Fed hiked 25bp, the CLARITY Act died in the Senate, and BTC still closed the week up nearly 6%. Then on Sunday, Saylor tweeted "a little more orange" and dropped another 950 BTC on Monday. Meanwhile, whales quietly rotated from BTC into ETH, and Strive added 1,355 BTC to its holdings.

_**Let’s get into it...**_


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6c53930f-b4d7-4e7d-baee-6a88bb56a6da/image.png?t=1781097813)
Caption: 

----------
# 🐋 THE BIG WHALE MOVES

### **1. Saylor Buys Another 950 BTC ("A Little More Orange")**

Strategy Inc. (formerly MicroStrategy)[ acquired](https://x.com/Strategy/status/2102005621910368432) 950 BTC for $75.7M during the week of[ Sep 14-20](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526396093/mstr-20260914.htm), per an 8-K filed Monday. That takes total holdings to 846,000 BTC, roughly 4.02% of the eventual 21M supply cap. Strategy also[ repurchased](https://blockonomi.com/strategy-bitcoin-holdings-reach-845050-btc-after-saylor-post) $174M of its variable-rate $STRC preferred stock in the same week, all funded from USD cash. No ATM equity issuance.

The buy came right after Saylor's cryptic "A Little More Orange" X post on Sunday, which posted Strategy's all-time BTC acquisition chart. Fans read the signal correctly. This is the second consecutive week Strategy retired preferred equity while adding BTC on the side.

**Whale Intel: **When the largest corporate BTC holder buys BOTH BTC and preferred stock in the same week with USD cash, it is a balance-sheet flex, not a stretch. Watch October for another buy.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/59932125-b963-4afb-b1a3-22e4743d202a/image.jpeg?t=1790142682)
Caption: Source: Strategy 8-K filing, Sept 21, 2026

### **2. The Great BTC → ETH Whale Rotation**

According to[ Lookonchain](https://x.com/lookonchain/status/2100835870219923791), 11 newly created wallets sold 602 BTC and bought 18,780 ETH ($45.83M) on Hyperliquid over three days. Wallet 0x4553[ swapped](https://x.com/lookonchain/status/2100055143576477869) 866 BTC for 26,924 ETH hours before the CLARITY vote on Sept 15. A third whale[ bought](https://x.com/lookonchain/status/2101860941113721332) 34,422 ETH ($86.5M) and staked all of it.

Прочитати на LinkedIn

Amid a changing employment landscape, 76% of millennial workers, currently ages 30 to 45, are actively questioning their career paths, according to Glassdoor data. Additionally, 68% say they’ve delayed a major life milestone due to career uncertainty.  This is a generation that should be familiar with disruption, since many came of age during the Great Recession and weathered mass layoffs during the global pandemic. But Chris Martin, Glassdoor’s senior economist, explains that today’s layoffs and AI disruption are even more disconcerting for millennials since they’re happening at a pivotal point in their careers. As a result, he says many millennials are taking a proactive approach to building a broader, more diversified professional foundation, which Glassdoor refers to as “stability stacking.” “Millennials are at the point in their career now where they should be the most stable,” Martin says. “They’ve reached management, an increasing number are approaching leadership positions where they’re in the C-Suite or VP or above. They’re reaching peak earnings as well. So there are all these things that are the hallmarks of a solid mid-career, but that’s just not what millennials are feeling.” I spoke to Martin, as well as millennial executive coach Janel Abrahami, about how millennials—as well as professionals of any generation—can “stability stack” their career to build some level of security in today’s market. Here’s a glimpse of what they had to say: Build your network: While creating a new side hustle may seem like an obvious step to stability stacking, Abrahami encourages professionals to not underestimate the impact of building opportune connections. “Maybe neither of you are sure on how you’ll work together in the beginning, but you kind of just know that you will,” she says. “And when that opportunity arises, at least you have that person on speed dial should you need to tap into them.” Stack your skills: With so much uncertainty around AI and how it will reshape certain roles, Martin says taking a skills-based approach to stability stacking could be a smart move. “Think about a couple of different skill-based responses where you can gain proficiency in AI-based skills or skills that are more resilient to AI replacement,” he suggests. This includes human skills such as effective communication, storytelling and adaptability.  Share your expertise
